title: ELF category and endianness are given by two independent flags
summary: In e_ident, EI_CLASS determines ELF32 or ELF64, and EI_DATA specifies the byte order of file data encoding.
applies: ELF file; System V Common ABI
detail: Before reading subsequent multibyte fields, the starting identification byte is used to identify both. 64-bit does not introduce little endian.
boundary: e_machine is another field; the same bit width and endianness do not uniquely identify an instruction set.
relevance: Explain the phenomenon that the file header magic number is correct but the section table offset reads an abnormally large number.
